title: How to Brew Green Tea (Without Making It Bitter)
meta_description: The secret to green tea is cooler water (165-185°F, never boiling) and a short steep — about 1 minute Japanese-style, or 3-4 minutes by general Western guidance. Here's the temperature, timing, and leaf amount that keep it from turning bitter.
keywords: how long to steep green tea
why is my green tea bitter
body_html:
The secret to good green tea is heat and time: use water around 165–185°F (74–85°C), never boiling, and steep about 1 minute by Japanese convention (Tea Association of the USA; Ippodo), or 3–4 minutes by general Western guidance (Healthline). Boiling water and long steeps are exactly what make green tea bitter. Use about 1 teaspoon of loose leaf (or one bag) per cup, and you'll get a sweet, fresh cup instead of an astringent one.

The green tea cheat sheet

VariableGreen tea targetWhy
Water temp165–185°F (74–85°C)Above this scorches the leaf and releases bitter catechins
Steep time~1 min (Japanese) or 3–4 min (Western)Longer over-extracts and turns astringent
Leaf amount~1 tsp (2 g) per cupMore leaf, shorter steep beats less leaf, longer steep
Re-steeps2–3 timesGood green leaves give several infusions

Getting the temperature right without a thermometer

Boil the kettle, then let it sit for 2–3 minutes before pouring — that drops boiling water into the green-tea range. Or add a splash of cold water to the cup first. The goal is hot, not scalding: if steam is billowing violently, it's too hot.

Why green tea goes bitter

Green tea is only lightly oxidized, so it keeps fresh catechins that taste smooth in cool water but harsh when scorched or over-steeped. Two fixes cover almost every bitter cup: lower the temperature and shorten the steep. For why green differs from black in the first place, see what is tea oxidation and green tea vs black tea.

Re-steeping

Quality loose green tea is a bargain because you can steep it 2–3 times. Add 15–30 seconds to each subsequent steep. For matcha, the rules are different — you whisk the whole powder rather than steep leaves; see matcha vs green tea. For every tea's ideal temperature, see our tea brewing temperature guide.

faqs.q: What temperature should green tea be brewed at?
faqs.a: Around 165-185°F (74-85°C) — hot but not boiling. Boiling water scorches the delicate leaf and pulls out bitter compounds. Let a boiled kettle rest 2-3 minutes before pouring.

faqs.q: How long should you steep green tea?
faqs.a: About 1 minute is the short Japanese sencha convention; general Western guidance is 3-4 minutes. Longer steeps over-extract and turn the cup astringent. If you want it stronger, use more leaf rather than pushing the steep past 4 minutes.

faqs.q: Why is my green tea bitter?
faqs.a: Almost always because the water was too hot or you steeped too long. Lower the temperature toward 165-175°F and try the shorter ~1 minute Japanese-style steep.
Yes — good loose green tea gives 2-3 infusions. Add about 15-30 seconds to each subsequent steep.
